findings.title: Materials' 59-point lens gap is extreme
findings.body: Materials sits at the 25th percentile on forward earnings but the 84th on trailing, a 59-point gap that dwarfs every other sector. The market is underwriting 111 percent earnings growth, which would be a historic re-rating of a sector whose trailing multiple is already rich.

findings.title: Health Care's forward percentile hits ceiling
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E is at the 100th percentile of its five-year range, up 22 points in a month, while its trailing multiple sits at the 87th. The 47 percent compression between the two lenses implies analysts expect 88 percent earnings growth, a bet that has pushed valuations to an absolute extreme.

findings.title: Energy's trailing richness contradicts forward cheapness
findings.body: Energy trades at the 36th percentile on forward earnings but the 84th on trailing, a 49-point gap. The 41 percent multiple compression implies 70 percent earnings growth, yet the forward percentile has been drifting cheaper over the past month, suggesting the market is not fully buying the rebound.
